svg.title: Host, client, server, data source, and the trust boundary between them
svg.desc: On the left a panel labeled Host contains a User box and a Model box above a Client sub-panel, with a note that the model picks the tool and the host asks you first. A dashed vertical line marked trust boundary separates the host from a Server panel on the right. An arrow marked tools slash call crosses the line to the server and an arrow marked result crosses back. Beyond the server, a dashed box marked Data source sits outside MCP, reached by your own driver rather than by the protocol. A caption states that every MCP message crosses the dashed line.
svg.text: Three roles, and the line the protocol runs along
The host owns every consent decision. The server cannot make one and cannot skip one.
Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, your own app
owns the transport and the request ids
a local process or a service
Owns the model, the conversation, and consent.
every MCP message crosses this line
